LESSON: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM ZINA (FORNICATION AND ADULTERY)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Values)
Topic 5.3: Prohibitions in Islam Zina (fornication and adultery)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Prohibitions in Islam Zina (fornication and adultery), part of Akhlaq (Moral Values) in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is zina prohibited in Islam? 2. How can a Muslim discourage zina in the society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the effects of zina in groups and present on charts/PowerPoints

2. watch or listen to video clips/read on the effects of zina (unwanted pregnancies, HIV and AIDS, Sexually Transmitted Diseases, family break-ups) and deduce lessons,

3. research on the rationale behind the 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the effects of zina in groups and present on charts/PowerPoints
2. watch or listen to video clips/read on the effects of zina (unwanted pregnancies, HIV and AIDS, Sexually Transmitted Diseases, family break-ups) and deduce lessons,
3. research on the rationale behind the 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Prohibitions in Islam Zina (fornication and adultery) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The skill of interacting with digital devices is enhanced as learners use digital devices to

research on the rationale behind the prohibition of zina and make notes.

• Critical thinking and problem-solving: the skill of research is enhanced as learners research on the rationale

behind the prohibition of zina.

• Communication and Collaboration: the skill of listening and speaking is enhanced as learners discuss and

present the measures put in place to curb zina.

Values:
Responsibility: enhanced as learners discuss the effects of zina in groups and present on charts/PowerPoints.
